policy.notice: This catalog describes compatibility claims. Runtime operations require a compiled model plugin or an explicitly enabled built-in capability profile. The models array retains legacy fan/power plugin states; builtin_capabilities describes the standalone Almighty LED and disk commands.

all_model_integration.priority: Complete the 25 current targets. DH2100 and DH2100+ are excluded by the user; do not continue legacy firmware searches.
all_model_integration.release_status: Expanded implementation is experimental and incomplete. Eight M.2 physical-slot layouts remain unknown; N76 supports explicit experimental userspace direct access with unverified outputs; the default sysfs path still needs a bound driver. GT has an explicit global FLOW holder lifecycle but requires active Host2EC. Fixture tests do not imply physical or distribution validation. DXP2800 GT SATA automatic routing is unknown without exact BIOS pairing; administrator calibration remains available.

led.identity: Exact DMI/revision or proven DT model plus compatible and full wiring. Each transport checks its own chip, driver binding or GPIO identity; family ID does not select protocol.
write_requirements: Controller owners excluded and fixed process lock held
Transport readback required; driver cache and unknown fields explicitly labelled
GPIO chardev writes require explicitly started ugreenctl-ledd to retain line ownership
GT FLOW=0 requires an explicit --takeover-flow holder lifecycle that restores all raw LEDs and original FLOW on clean exit
N76 direct exception explicitly accepted 2026-10-27: only mode registers verified, output/PWM/timing unknown and sent-unverified; no guessed readback
known_gaps: DH2600/DXP480T Plus default to bound-driver sysfs. Explicit --n76-direct BUS:ADDR provides experimental byte-data control without the vendor module. True output/PWM/timing readback remains unknown, declared sent-unverified by user choice; no identify/locate restoration or physical validation.

DXP2800 GT requires CS2011, already active LDN0a and a valid dynamic Host2EC base. Direct CLI requires FLOW=1; explicit ugreenctl-ledd --takeover-flow handles a verified FLOW=0 lifecycle. Inactive LDN is unsupported; autonomous animation phase and physical ARGB read feasibility remain unverified.
DH2300 and DH4300 Plus need exact original DT wiring and a GPIO v2 kernel, or the verified stock driver. GPIO holder is explicitly started by the user.
DXP2800 accepts only its two independently evidenced product_version strings.

disk_mapping.transport: Read-only Linux sysfs; complete controller roles/local ATA ports, exact PCI bridge/root paths, or verified ARM OF topology
disk_mapping.firmware_conditional_topology_scope: At least one physical-slot interface has a conditional rule; this does not imply every interface is mapped. See per_model and unknown_m2_physical_slot_models. Physical-slot mapping and independently controllable bay LEDs are separate capabilities.
disk_mapping.conditional_requirements: Exact model/revision; independently evidenced full controllers and empty ports; exact PCI/OF roles; no extra, missing or ambiguous topology; GT SATA BIOS revision gate. block_name alone never gives physical slot.
disk_mapping.calibration: Root-owned non-symlink physical topology file, exact model, no group/other write permission or duplicate slots/topologies
disk_mapping.unknown_mapping_behavior: Inventory remains available; disk locate refuses unmapped or ambiguous selectors

non_applicable.DH2300: No NVMe group in the official storage table
non_applicable.DH4300 Plus: No NVMe group in the official storage table
non_applicable.DXP480T Plus: No SATA group or independent NVMe bay LEDs; its four physical NVMe slots are conditionally mapped

disk_mapping.nvme_namespaces: Namespaces under one live canonical PCIe controller with consistent identity/mapping represent one physical disk. Every namespace path and WWID remains selectable; namespace numbering never selects a physical slot.
disk_mapping.scan_consistency: Recheck whole-block candidate membership, identities and topology before returning. A hotplug change, including a newly visible but uninitialized NVMe member, fails the scan and requires a rescan.
disk_mapping.bios_routing_policy: No LL_/else default for GT2800 SATA. Only rules identical in both official revisions retained independently; unknown SATA also blocks shared U.2 LED mapping.

wake.rtc_model_identity: Independent exact-model table in models/wake_profiles.c; never inferred from WOL capability

controller.transport: Linux hwmon with guarded direct Super I/O fallback

known_conflicts: The vendor /proc/it86 interface or ug_it86x_cpufan module must not access the controller concurrently.
Direct fallback is available only after the it87 module is unloaded and requires --force --apply.
Wake-on-LAN follows the stock eth0/eth1 map and requires --force --apply until it is physically validated.

evidence.method: Clean-room observation of the vendor module interface and validation of the IT8613 identity/access sequence.
evidence.scope: CPU and system fan PWM/status; AC recovery startup policy; stock hwmonitor-480t magic-packet WOL on eth0 and eth1.

controller.transport: Linux hwmon with guarded direct Super I/O fallback

known_conflicts: The vendor /proc/it86 interface or ug_it86x_sio module must not access the controller concurrently.
The generic it87 driver may remain loaded while its name=it8613 hwmon node is used; it must be unloaded before direct fallback.

evidence.method: Static clean-room reverse engineering of ug_it86x-sio.ko plus the DXP4800S branch in ug-load-drive.sh and hwmonitor.
evidence.scope: Exact DMI branch; IT8613 identity/access sequence; single sysfan1 tachometer and PWM path; AC recovery registers; stock user-space automatic fan policy; generic hwmonitor magic-packet WOL on eth0 and eth1. No physical write validation.

evidence.method: Exact DMI routing, ELF symbols/relocations/disassembly, and dxp4800s.conf; see docs/DXP4800S_1.19.md.
evidence.scope: Reconfirms single IT8613 fan and AC recovery mapping; dedicated stock config preserves stock-4800s thresholds. No physical validation.

write_requirements: --apply for hwmon writes; --force --apply for direct fallback writes

controller.transport: Linux hwmon with guarded direct Super I/O fallback

known_conflicts: The vendor /proc/it86 interface or ug_it86x_cpufan module must not access the controller concurrently.
Direct fallback is available only after the it87 module is unloaded and requires --force --apply.

evidence.method: Static clean-room reverse engineering of the DXP480T Plus branch in ug_it86x-cpufan.ko.
evidence.scope: Three tachometer paths; CPU command at 0x17/0x73; stock system-pair set command at 0x16/0x6b then 0x1e/0x7b; AC recovery path; hwmonitor-480t magic-packet WOL on eth0 and eth1.

evidence.method: Physical DXP480T Plus report supplied to the LLLED_FPK project on 2026-07-22.
evidence.scope: CPU control responded but both system fans did not. This matches the prior fallback incorrectly writing the CPU 0x17/0x73 path for both targets. The corrected firmware-reversed system-pair map awaits controlled physical validation.
N76E003 I2C/SMBus LED MCU identified; no LED write protocol exposed.

evidence.method: Read-only physical DXP480T Plus report supplied to the LLLED_FPK project on 2026-07-23.
evidence.scope: One wired PCI Ethernet controller was present: Aquantia AQC113 at 0000:73:00.0, renamed enp115s0. The atlantic driver reported Supports Wake-on: pg and Wake-on: g. With the stock eth0/eth1 names absent, only this exact model accepts one renamed physical PCI Ethernet interface; magic-packet wake after shutdown is still unvalidated.

controller.transport: Linux hwmon with guarded direct Super I/O fallback; Linux ethtool for WOL

known_conflicts: The vendor /proc/it86 interface, ug_it86x_sio module, or stock hwmonitor service must not access the Super I/O controller concurrently.
The generic it87 driver may remain loaded while its name=it8613 hwmon node is used; it must be unloaded before direct fan fallback.
The firmware establishes eth0 and eth1 for WOL; if both names are absent, the shared resolver requires exactly two physical PCI Ethernet adapters and rejects any other count.
The bound leds_mcu_28a48 driver owns the LED MCU; direct I2C writes are not exposed.

evidence.method: User-reported physical validation with LLLED_FPK 2.1.2 on fnOS kernel 6.18.18.c1032-trim.
evidence.scope: Exact DMI DX4600: fan control, AC-power recovery and Wake-on-LAN confirmed working. DX4600+/Pro and per-policy/per-port details are not covered. Existing identity, locking and write guards remain required.

evidence.method: Static clean-room reverse engineering of the official DX4600 routes in hwmonitor.sh, ug-load-drive.sh, dx4600.conf, hwmonitor, ug_it86x-sio.ko, and the firmware product tables.
evidence.scope: Exact DX4600, DX4600+, and DX4600 Pro product strings; one system-fan IT8613 path; AC-recovery registers; stock mode-2 user-space fan curve; magic-packet WOL on eth0 and eth1. No physical write validation.
